title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Cheese, mustard, and ale sauce grilled on toast
excerpt: A thick, deeply savoury cheese sauce made with cheddar, ale, Worcestershire sauce, and mustard, spooned over thick toast and grilled until bubbling. Not cheese on toast: the sauce is made separately and is considerably better.

recipe.sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit appears in British cookbooks from the early eighteenth century, usually under the name Welsh rabbit, a name of uncertain origin. Hannah Glasse's recipe (1747) is one of the earliest printed versions. The dish became a staple of British supper and pub cooking through the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The key distinction from simple melted cheese on toast is the sauce: cheese is melted into ale and bound with egg yolk or flour, then grilled.

content.text: Use a strongly flavoured mature cheddar: mild cheese gives a bland rarebit. The ale should be a bitter or a pale ale; strong stouts can be bitter in the sauce. Grate the cheese finely so it melts smoothly. The sauce should be thick enough to hold its shape on the toast; if it is too runny, it will run off the edges before it has time to blister under the grill.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the ale and milk, whisking constantly, and stir until smooth and thick, 3 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Add the cheese, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir until the cheese is fully melted and the sauce is smooth. Stir in the egg yolk. Season with black pepper. The sauce will be thick and glossy.

Heat the grill to high. Toast the bread on one side only. Flip the toast and spoon the cheese sauce thickly onto the untoasted side, spreading it right to the edges. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden and blistered in places. Serve immediately.
